vms.forceStopDescription: The VM is turned off without shutting down its OS. Unsaved data in the guest is lost.

reason.powerPending: A power action is still in progress.
reason.reverting: Not available while a snapshot is being reverted.
reason.busy: The VM is starting or stopping.

vms.deleteDescription: The VM is deleted. Its volumes are kept.
vms.deleteSnapshots_other: Also delete all {{count}} of its snapshots
vms.hasSnapshots: A VM with snapshots cannot be deleted. Delete its snapshots first, or check the box to delete them along with the VM.
vms.snapshotsPending: A snapshot of this VM is still being taken. Delete the VM once it is done.
vms.deletingSnapshots: Deleting the snapshots one at a time. This cannot be cancelled once started.

snapshots.createDescription: Saves the VM's disks, firmware variables and settings so you can return to this point later.
snapshots.includeMemoryHint: Also saves the running state. Reverting resumes the VM where it was.
snapshots.unsupported: Only VMs whose disks are all qcow2 can take snapshots. {{volume}} is {{format}}.
snapshots.busy: The VM is starting or stopping. Snapshots can be taken, reverted and deleted once it settles.
snapshots.revertDescription: The current state of {{vm}} is lost. The VM is powered off, then its disks, firmware variables and settings return to the snapshot. It stays off.
snapshots.revertDescriptionMemory: The current state of {{vm}} is lost. The VM is powered off, then its disks, firmware variables and settings return to the snapshot, and it resumes running from the saved memory.
snapshots.deleteDescription: The snapshot is deleted. Snapshots taken after it are kept, and the VM's current state does not change.

errors.exists: This VM already has a snapshot with this name.

scheduleError.vm_busy: Skipped because the VM was busy; it will try again later.
scheduleError.node_offline: Skipped because the VM's node is offline ({{message}}).

clone.title: Clone {{name}}
clone.description: A new stopped VM is made with full copies of the disks. It gets new MAC addresses and no snapshot schedule.
clone.name: New VM name
clone.running: The VM is not stopped. Stop it first or choose a snapshot.
clone.busy: The VM is starting or stopping. Try again when it has settled.
clone.gone: The chosen snapshot no longer exists or is not ready. Choose another source.

errors.exists: A VM with this name already exists.

forms.name: Use 1–63 lowercase letters, digits and -, not starting or ending with -.

volumes.createDescription: A new disk image in a storage pool. A qcow2 volume takes space only as it is written.
volumes.deleteDescription: The disk image and all data on it are deleted.
volumes.resizeDescription: Volumes can only grow. A running VM sees the new size right away; grow the partition and file system inside the guest yourself.

errors.exists: A volume with this name already exists.
errors.grow: Enter a size larger than the current size.

reason.inUse: Remove it from the VM first.
reason.vmsUnknown: Cannot tell which VMs use it.

uploads.title: Upload a disk image
uploads.description: The file goes to the node you are connected to ({{node}}), so only storage pools on that node can be chosen. The image is converted into a new volume.
uploads.noPool: No storage pool is available on this node.
uploads.noResponse: {{name}}: no response from the server. Check the volume list for the result.
uploads.dropped: The server rejected the upload or the connection was lost.
uploads.noNode: Cannot tell which node you are connected to. {{error}}

pools.createDescription: A directory on the nodes that holds volume files. Create the directory on each node first.
pools.pathHint: An absolute path on the nodes.
pools.nodesHint: Leave all unchecked to use it on every node.
pools.deleteDescription: Only the pool is removed. Files in its directory stay on the nodes.

errors.nodesGone: The chosen nodes are no longer in the cluster. Choose again.

networks.userNote: The user network (QEMU NAT) is always available and is not listed.
networks.createDescription: Points VM interfaces at a Linux bridge that already exists on the nodes. VMs on this network run only on nodes with the bridge.
networks.deleteDescription: Only the network is removed. The bridges on the nodes are not changed.

errors.reserved: The name user is reserved for NAT.

nodes.joinNote: To add a node, issue a join token on the Cluster page and run oplctl cluster join on the new node.
nodes.maintenanceNote: No new VMs are placed on a node in maintenance. VMs already running there keep running.
nodes.removeDescription: Only for a node that is dead for good. It cannot rejoin with its current data, and VMs assigned to it stay assigned.
nodes.removeNote: Only offline nodes can be removed here. To remove a live node, run oplctl cluster leave on it.

reason.thisNode: You are connected through this node.
reason.online: The node is online. Run oplctl cluster leave on it.

accounts.changePasswordDescription: All your sessions end. Sign in again with the new password.
accounts.passwordChanged: Your password was changed. Sign in with the new password.

users.roleHint: Operators change VMs and volumes. Viewers only read. Neither can see accounts.
users.passwordDescription: The user's sessions end and they sign in with the new password.
users.deleteDescription: The user and their API tokens are deleted.
users.selfNote: Change your own password from the account menu. Only another administrator can change your role or delete your account.

reason.selfRole: Only another administrator can change your role.
reason.selfPassword: Change your own password from the account menu.
reason.selfDelete: Only another administrator can delete your account.

tokens.note: Scripts and tools use API tokens. A token has the role of its owner. oplctl login makes one for the CLI.
tokens.createDescription: The token acts as you, with your role.
tokens.secretDescription: Copy the token now. It cannot be shown again.
tokens.deleteDescription: Anything using the token stops working right away.

cluster.title: Cluster {{name}}
cluster.caNote: Every node's HTTPS certificate is signed by the cluster CA. Import the CA into your browser to stop the certificate warning, and check that its fingerprint matches. Browsers show the SHA-256 fingerprint in uppercase hex, in pairs separated by colons or spaces; compare it with the hex after sha256: (letter case does not matter).
cluster.membersNote: Voters keep the cluster state. A learner is a node that is still joining.
cluster.issueDescription: A new node joins with the token once. Start opld on the new node first.
cluster.issuedDescription: Run this on the new node before {{time}}. It cannot be shown again.
cluster.commandNote: Add --socket if opld on the new node does not use /run/opl/opld.sock.

vmForm.runningNote: The VM is running: its node and disks cannot change. Other changes apply from the next start.

vmForm.scheduleMemoryHint: Memory is saved only while the VM is running and has disks.
